input.note:
**Root Cause: AWS On-Demand vCPU quota exhausted — Cluster Autoscaler cannot provision new nodes.**

**Evidence observed:**
- All 8 `feature-backfill` pods in `ml-batch` are `Pending` and unscheduled (no node assigned).
- Each pod requests **12 CPUs** and targets the `batch-c6i-4xl` EKS node group (c6i.4xlarge = 16 vCPUs each).
- Pod scheduler message: *"0/12 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient cpu, 10 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector."* The 2 existing nodes in the group are already under-capacity; the other 10 nodes in the cluster don't match the `eks.amazonaws.com/nodegroup: batch-c6i-4xl` node selector.
- Cluster Autoscaler correctly triggered a scale-up from 2 → 10 nodes in the `batch-c6i-4xl` group, but both attempts (at ~00:04 and ~02:11) failed with the same AWS error: **`VcpuLimitExceeded — current On-Demand vCPU limit is 256`**.

**Why this is happening now:** The AWS account has hit its regional On-Demand vCPU service quota for the Standard instance bucket (A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z — which includes c6i). Adding the 8 new nodes (8 × 16 = 128 vCPUs) would exceed the 256-vCPU cap given existing cluster usage. Until the quota is raised, the Autoscaler will continue to fail and the pods will remain Pending indefinitely [cite: tasks/debug/debug-application/debug-pods#debugging-pods-1] [cite: concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers#my-pods-are-pending-with-event-message-failedscheduling-1].

**Fix — action required from the Cloud Platform team (AWS console access needed):**
1. **Request a vCPU quota increase** via AWS Service Quotas: open the AWS Console → Service Quotas → EC2 → *"Running On-Demand Standard (A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z) instances"* and request an increase sufficient to cover peak cluster demand. Alternatively, use the link in the AWS error message: https://aws.amazon.com/contact-us/ec2-request
2. As a **short-term workaround** (if the quota increase will take time), the team could reduce the Job's `parallelism` so fewer nodes are needed simultaneously — e.g. running 4 pods at a time requires only 4 additional c6i.4xlarge nodes (64 vCPUs) which may fit within the current headroom.
3. Optionally, consider adding a second instance type (e.g. m6i.4xlarge) to the node group as a fallback, which may draw from separate capacity pools.

**Action for ticket owner:** File a request with the Cloud Platform team to raise the On-Demand Standard vCPU quota in the affected AWS region (us-east-1). No changes to your Kubernetes manifests are needed.
